segments.t: The integrated SFTP Manager provides a graphical file manager for transferring files between your local machine and remote servers via SFTP. It features a dual-panel layout, full file operations support, and seamless integration with the Snippet Editor for remote file editing.
You can open the SFTP Manager in two ways:

KTPH006Menu:KTPH007 KTPH008Connections → SFTP-Client...KTPH009 (KTPH010KTPH000KTPH011+KTPH012KTPH001KTPH013+KTPH014KTPH002KTPH015, on macOS KTPH016KTPH003KTPH017+KTPH018KTPH004KTPH019+KTPH020KTPH005KTPH021). With a connected terminal tab in front, it opens for that tab's server; otherwise you pick a connection first.
KTPH000Dashboard:KTPH001 right-click a connected session KTPH004 KTPH002SFTP-Client...KTPH003
If the connection uses a temporary SSH key that has expired, you will be prompted to enter a new key before the connection can proceed.
The SFTP Manager uses a KTPH000two-panel layoutKTPH001 for easy side-by-side file management:
Both panels display the same columns, all of which are sortable by clicking the column header:
File size in human-readable format (directories show —); sorting uses the exact byte count, with folders first
Owner name (local: from filesystem; remote: from SFTP or UID)
Group name (local: from filesystem; remote: from SFTP or GID)
By default, files are sorted by the KTPH000TypeKTPH001 column in this order:
KTPH001Parent directoryKTPH002 (KTPH000) — always at the top
KTPH002Directories starting with "."KTPH003 (e.g., KTPH000, KTPH001) — alphabetically

Click any column header to sort by that column. Clicking the Type column again toggles between ascending and descending order. The parent directory (KTPH000) stays at the top whichever column and direction you sort by.

Remote folders are read in the background, so the window stays responsive even for a folder with tens of thousands of entries. While a folder loads, a KTPH000Loading…KTPH001 indicator covers the remote list. The path field and the list switch to the new folder only once it has been read; if it cannot be read (it does not exist, or you lack the rights), an error is shown and the folder you were in stays.

Type a path into the remote KTPH008PathKTPH009 field and press KTPH010KTPH007KTPH011 to go there. KTPH000 and KTPH001 stand for your login directory on the server, and a path without a leading KTPH002 is taken relative to the folder shown; KTPH003 and KTPH004 are resolved, so KTPH005 opens the sibling folder KTPH006.

When the server or the network ends the session, the status bar shows KTPH000Disconnected fromKTPH001 KTPH002hostKTPH003 with a KTPH004ReconnectKTPH005 button, and the remote actions are disabled. If the connection drops without the server saying so, the first remote action you try (Refresh, Upload, Download and so on) brings up the same state instead of doing nothing.

KTPH000ReconnectKTPH001 opens a new session with the same credentials and lists the folder you were in. The server's host key is checked as on the first connect: an unchanged key connects without a prompt, a changed key is still blocked.

SFTP Manager tabs are saved with a KTPH000projectKTPH001. Opening the project with KTPH002Auto-ReconnectKTPH003 reconnects each tab at the local and remote folders it was in when you saved. A folder that no longer exists opens the home folder instead; on the remote side the status bar says so.
Each panel has its own group of toolbar buttons below the lists (local on the left, remote on the right) and a right-click context menu:
Select local files or folders and click KTPH000UploadKTPH001, or drag them onto the remote panel; see KTPH002Drag and dropKTPH003
Select remote files or folders and click KTPH000DownloadKTPH001, or drag them onto the local panel
Select one entry and press KTPH001KTPH000KTPH002, or choose KTPH003RenameKTPH004 in the context menu. An existing entry of the new name is never replaced; you get an error instead

Click the folder button next to KTPH000RefreshKTPH001, or choose KTPH002New FolderKTPH003 in the context menu, in either panel. The folder is created in the folder shown; a name that already exists is an error

Select entries and click KTPH005DeleteKTPH006, choose KTPH007DeleteKTPH008 in the context menu, or press KTPH009KTPH000KTPH010 (KTPH011KTPH001KTPH012+KTPH013KTPH002KTPH014, on macOS KTPH015KTPH003KTPH016+KTPH017KTPH004KTPH018). You confirm before anything is deleted

KTPH000Copy to...KTPH001 in the context menu copies within the same side: locally into a folder you pick (in the background), remotely into a folder path you type. A remote folder copied where a folder of that name exists merges into it; copying an item onto itself or into one of its own subfolders is refused with an error
Select exactly one local or remote file, then use the KTPH000EditKTPH001 toolbar menu or the right-click context menu
KTPH000ArchiveKTPH001 in the remote toolbar, or KTPH002Archive...KTPH003 in either context menu, packs the selection as ZIP, TAR.BZ2 or 7z, depending on the tools available on that side
Select entries, then click KTPH000RightsKTPH001 or choose KTPH002Set Owner/Permissions...KTPH003 in the context menu. Separate fields for User, Group, and octal permissions (e.g., 755)

A name for KTPH004RenameKTPH005 or KTPH006New FolderKTPH007 must be a single entry in the folder shown: it may not be empty, KTPH000 or KTPH001, or contain KTPH002 or KTPH003. The dialog stays open with an error until the name is usable.

You can drag entries between the two panels, from your desktop into the SFTP Manager, and in small amounts from the server to your desktop. While you drag, the panel or the folder row that would take the drop is highlighted; dropping on a folder row puts the entries into that folder, dropping anywhere else into the folder shown.
Local rows onto the remote panel
Uploaded, as with KTPH000UploadKTPH001: a folder merges, and a file of the same name on the server is not replaced without asking (see KTPH002When a file already existsKTPH003)
Files from Finder, Explorer or the file browser sidebar onto the remote panel
Remote rows onto the local panel
Downloaded in the background, as with KTPH000DownloadKTPH001: folders included, and a local file of the same name is not replaced without asking
Files from Finder, Explorer or the file browser sidebar onto the local panel
Copied in the background; a name that is already there gets a number, as in KTPH000, and a file dropped onto the folder it is in is left alone
Local rows onto the desktop or another program
Remote rows onto the desktop or another program
Only for at most 20 files with at most 16 MB together, and no folders
A drag into the same panel does nothing; use KTPH000Copy to...KTPH001 or KTPH002RenameKTPH003 there.
Dragging from the server to the desktop

The desktop can only take files that already exist when the drag starts. korTTY therefore downloads the dragged remote files into a private temporary folder first, which can hold the window for up to 5 seconds. Folders, more than 20 files, more than 16 MB or a download that takes longer can only be dropped inside the window; the status bar says so, and you drop them on the local panel instead. A download that runs out of time stops in the middle of its file and deletes what it wrote, so it does not go on filling the temporary folder in the background. A link on the server counts as the file it points to, so a link to a large file is not offered to the desktop either. The temporary copies are deleted when you start the next drag or close the tab.
These keys work in both panels:
KTPH005KTPH000KTPH006 or KTPH007KTPH001KTPH008+KTPH009KTPH002KTPH010 (KTPH011KTPH003KTPH012+KTPH013KTPH004KTPH014 on macOS, in the list)

Upload copies the selected local files and folders into the remote folder that was shown when you clicked KTPH001UploadKTPH002; browsing elsewhere while it runs does not change the target. Upload stays disabled until the first remote folder has been listed, because the server does not expand KTPH000 itself.
KTPH000Uploading a folder again mergesKTPH001 into the existing remote folder: other remote files are kept, and for each file that already exists korTTY asks what to do (see below).
KTPH000Files are streamedKTPH001, so their size is not limited by memory; files larger than 2 GB upload like any other.

If the connection drops during an upload or download, the unfinished items fail as KTPH000Connection lostKTPH001 with one KTPH002DisconnectedKTPH003 state rather than an error dialog per file; after KTPH004ReconnectKTPH005, select them in the KTPH006transfer listKTPH007 and click KTPH008RetryKTPH009.

KTPH000Linked folders are not followed.KTPH001 A symbolic link to a file is transferred with the file's content; a link to a folder is skipped and named in the summary at the end, so a link loop cannot make a transfer run forever.

KTPH012Downloaded names stay inside the target folder.KTPH013 A server name such as KTPH000 or KTPH001 is refused. On Windows, names that Windows reserves for devices (KTPH002, KTPH003, KTPH004, KTPH005, KTPH006 to KTPH007, KTPH008 to KTPH009, also with an extension such as KTPH010) and names that end in a dot or a space or contain KTPH011 are refused too, because Windows would write them somewhere else or change them.

Uploads and downloads run in the background, up to three files at a time (KTPH000Settings → SFTP Manager → KTPH001Parallel transfersKTPH002KTPH003, 1 to 8), each over its own SFTP channel. The first transfer opens the KTPH004TransfersKTPH005 list at the bottom of the tab; the arrow on its left collapses it to its header. Each row is a file or folder you transferred, with its direction, a progress bar, the bytes so far, the speed and the time left; a folder row adds up the files in it. The status bar shows how many files of all running transfers are done and the overall speed, and says KTPH006Upload completeKTPH007 or KTPH008Download completeKTPH009 when a batch is finished.
Stops the selected rows; a cancelled file leaves no partial file behind, unless the settings keep it for a later resume
Starts the selected failed or cancelled rows again; for a folder, only what did not arrive
Stops every transfer, including an open KTPH000File already existsKTPH001 question
Removes the rows that are done, skipped or cancelled; failed rows stay for a retry

KTPH000Failures no longer open one error dialog per file.KTPH001 A failed file gets a red row of its own (also when it is inside a folder you transferred), the reason is in its KTPH002StateKTPH003 column, and once the batch is finished one summary window lists the failed files and the linked folders that were not followed. The summary does not block the tab.
KTPH000The lists follow the transfers.KTPH001 When files arrive in the folder a panel shows, that panel is listed again shortly afterwards; a folder you browsed away from is not.

KTPH001Files arrive complete or not at all.KTPH002 A file is first written as KTPH000 next to the target and gets its real name only once it is complete, so an interrupted transfer never leaves a half-written file under the real name. The one exception is replacing a server file that belongs to another user, which is written in place (see KTPH003When a file already existsKTPH004).

KTPH000Interrupted transfers continue where they stopped.KTPH001 After a failure or a lost connection, KTPH002RetryKTPH003 continues an unfinished file instead of starting over; see KTPH004Resuming interrupted transfersKTPH005.

KTPH000Closing the tab asks while transfers run.KTPH001 The tab's close button, KTPH002File KTPH014 Close TabKTPH003, KTPH004Close All TabsKTPH005, closing the window and quitting korTTY first ask KTPH006Cancel KTPH007nKTPH008 running transfers and close?KTPH009; KTPH010Keep tab openKTPH011 is the default and leaves every transfer running. Closing cancels the transfers that are not finished and deletes their partial files, unless KTPH012Settings → SFTP ManagerKTPH013 keeps the partial files of cancelled transfers. Finished or failed rows ask nothing, and the automatic closing of idle tabs waits until the transfers are done.

KTPH001Leftover partial filesKTPH002 are shown in italics, with a tooltip. KTPH003Remove leftover partial filesKTPH004 at the end of either panel's context menu deletes the KTPH000 files in the folder shown after a confirmation; partial files of transfers that are still running are left alone.

A transfer that fails, or whose connection is lost, keeps its KTPH000 file, and KTPH001RetryKTPH002 (after KTPH003ReconnectKTPH004, if the connection was lost) continues it from where it stopped. While it continues, its KTPH005StateKTPH006 column says KTPH007ContinuingKTPH008.

KTPH000Only when nothing has changed.KTPH001 korTTY remembers the size and modification time of the source when the transfer starts. If the source is different on the retry, the partial file is larger than the source, or the last 64 KB before the resume point no longer match the source, the partial file is removed and the file is copied from the beginning.

KTPH000Only your own partial files.KTPH001 On the server a partial file is continued only when it is still a plain file owned by the user you are logged in as; a link or a file of another user at that name is never written to. On your computer the partial file is never followed through a link either. A partial file korTTY did not leave for this very transfer (another tab, another computer or another user may be writing it right now) is neither continued nor removed: the transfer fails with a message naming the file, and you remove a real leftover with KTPH002Remove leftover partial filesKTPH003.

KTPH000Cancel removes the partial fileKTPH001 unless KTPH002Settings → SFTP Manager → KTPH003Keep the partial file when a transfer is cancelledKTPH004KTPH005 is on. With KTPH006Resume interrupted transfersKTPH007 switched off there, every unfinished partial file is removed and a retry always starts over.

KTPH001What korTTY stores.KTPH002 The remembered sizes and times are kept in KTPH000 in korTTY's configuration folder, readable only by you. An entry holds a fingerprint of the connection and the two paths, not the paths or host names themselves, and never file content; entries of transfers you never retried are dropped after 30 days. The file is not part of the configuration backup, because the partial files it describes stay on this computer and its servers.
KTPH000Leftover partial filesKTPH001 of transfers you gave up on can be removed with KTPH002Remove leftover partial filesKTPH003 in either panel's context menu (see KTPH004Transfer listKTPH005).

An upload or download never replaces an existing file silently. When the target folder already has an entry of the same name, korTTY shows KTPH000File already existsKTPH001 with the size and modification time of both sides (the later time is marked as newer) and these choices:
The existing file is replaced by the transferred one
The existing entry is left alone and this item is not transferred
The item is transferred under a free name with a number, such as KTPH000; a double extension stays together (KTPH001), and a dotfile gets the number at the end (KTPH002)
The rest of the batch stops; closing the dialog or pressing KTPH001KTPH000KTPH002 does the same

KTPH000Do this for all remaining conflicts of this kindKTPH001 answers every later conflict of the same kind in that batch without asking again. The kinds are kept apart: replacing all files never replaces a symbolic link or a folder.
KTPH000A folder onto a folder of the same name mergesKTPH001 without asking; only the files inside it can conflict.

KTPH000A symbolic link is never replaced.KTPH001 When the existing entry is a link, only KTPH002SkipKTPH003 and KTPH004Keep bothKTPH005 are offered, so a transfer cannot write through a link to a file somewhere else.
KTPH000A file and a folder cannot replace each other.KTPH001 When one side is a file and the other a folder, only KTPH002SkipKTPH003 and KTPH004Keep bothKTPH005 are offered.

KTPH000A file owned by another user is written in place.KTPH001 When the existing remote file belongs to another user, the dialog says so; replacing it writes into the file directly, so its owner and permissions stay as they are.

KTPH000One question at a time.KTPH001 When several files of a batch conflict at once, korTTY asks about one of them and waits with the others, so an answer for all of them arrives before the next question. Closing the tab answers an open question with KTPH002Cancel transferKTPH003.

KTPH000The question can be answered in advance.KTPH001 KTPH002Settings → SFTP Manager → KTPH003When the target already existsKTPH004KTPH005 can skip existing files or overwrite them without asking; links and file/folder mismatches are still asked about. An organization can set this choice for you.

On a computer whose disk ignores upper and lower case (the macOS and Windows default), a name that differs only in case counts as the same name, both for the question and for the numbered name KTPH000Keep bothKTPH001 picks.
When file transfer is turned off by your organizationKTPH000

An organization can switch file transfer off with its KTPH002enterprise policyKTPH003 (KTPH000). The SFTP Manager then still opens and browses the server, and renaming, deleting, permissions, archives, search and copying on the server keep working, but KTPH004UploadKTPH005, KTPH006DownloadKTPH007 and KTPH008RetryKTPH009 in the transfer list are greyed out, dragging files onto the server panel or server files onto the local panel is not accepted (the pointer shows no copy symbol), and remote files cannot be dragged to the desktop. Files from the desktop can still be dropped onto the local panel. JobScheduler jobs that upload, download or sync with SFTP, and rsync jobs, fail with the same message without connecting. Commands such as KTPH001 typed into a terminal are not affected.

The permissions field of KTPH003Set Owner/PermissionsKTPH004 and of the remote archive dialog accepts exactly three octal digits, such as KTPH000 or KTPH001; leave it empty (or unchanged) to keep the current mode. Anything else keeps the dialog open with an error, so no other text ever reaches KTPH002.

The file-mode buttons provide these save choices:
KTPH000Overwrite fileKTPH001 — writes the current editor content back to the original local or remote file
KTPH000Save as...KTPH001 — writes a new local file through a file chooser, or for remote files prompts for a new file name in the same remote directory
KTPH000Save as snippetKTPH001 — stores the current content as a new Snippet Manager snippet without marking the source file as saved

The search field above each list filters the folder shown as you type, without leaving it; the parent entry KTPH000 stays visible. korTTY evaluates the wildcards itself, the same way for local and remote names. A pattern with a wildcard has to match the whole name, ignoring case:
KTPH000 finds all log files, KTPH001 all names starting with "backup"
One of the listed characters; KTPH000 or KTPH001 one that is not listed
KTPH000 finds names starting with a or b
KTPH000 finds Python and shell files
Text without a wildcard matches anywhere in the name, ignoring case: KTPH000 finds KTPH001. A pattern that cannot be read, such as an unclosed KTPH002, is searched for as plain text.
